newsitem.title: USA: Americans concerned about money in politics.
newsitem.headline: Americans concerned about money in politics.

text.p: Two-thirds of Americans believe their own elected representatives were more likely to be responsive to large political contributors than their constituents, according to a new poll released Friday.

The poll of 1,404 adults, conducted for the non-partisan Centre for Responsive Politics by Princeton Survey Research Associates, also found that 76 percent of respondents thought elected officials cared more about getting re-elected than about doing what was best for the country.

"This poll should be a wake-up call for elected officials who think voters don't care about this issue. Voters do care and they feel their elected officials don't care enough," said Kent Cooper, the center's executive director.
In other findings, two-thirds said excessive influence of political contributions was a major problem for the system. The poll carried a three percentage point margin of error.
The survey found little difference between the views of Republicans and Democrats and voters were equally disenchanted with both parties.
Some 71 percent said Republicans and Democrats were equally likely to engage in questionable fund raising, despite a flood of publicity mainly focused on Democratic practices in the 1996 elections.
